paper.purpose: The folio itself, and the text colour on any blue-gray field.

paper-band.purpose: The marginal endorsement column, ruled text areas and selects, scrollbar track.

paper-deep.purpose: Inset wells, and the margin cell under row hover.

ink.purpose: All content: headings, entry names, figures. Measured 15.54:1 on ledger bone.

ink-2.purpose: Captions, meta lines, dates, placeholders. Warm, tinted from ink, never a neutral gray. Measured 6.32:1.

ink-3.purpose: Disabled controls, and the drawn hairline meaning 'nothing endorsed against this entry'. Never running text.

rule.purpose: Every division, column rule, column head, label, stamp and icon. Structure and interaction. Measured 6.61:1 on ledger bone.

rule-strong.purpose: Heavy 2px division rules, the registry head band, filled primary actions, selection, caret, the focus bracket. Paper on this field measures 9.71:1.

rule-hair.purpose: Column and row divisions, feint ruling on a waiting folio. An alpha derivation of rule-strong; no tonal ramp — it is a transparency, not a step.

rule-wash.purpose: Hover on an entry or a ruled button. An alpha derivation of rule-strong.

vermilion.purpose: Struck, cancelled, or in error. Nothing else, ever. Measured 5.45:1 on ledger bone and 5.01:1 on the struck row band.

vermilion-band.purpose: The wash under a struck row and behind a danger button on hover. An alpha derivation of vermilion.

figure.purpose: The ramp's top step: page h1, return values, the standing-obligation count.

head.purpose: A division head (h2) and a slip's own title. h3 drops to body size.

entry.purpose: The proprietor's name on a register entry, and every text input — you write at entry size.

body.purpose: Running prose, capped at 68ch (60ch on the standing line).

caption.purpose: Notices, terms, in-row dates, toast copy.

micro.purpose: Endorsement dates, folio meta, admin email, operator email in the head.

stamp.purpose: Tracked caps in the rule colour: column heads, field labels, buttons, nav links, badges, section heads. The most-used role in the system.

fonts.source: self-hosted variable woff2, weights 400-700, two subsets (latin, latin-ext), declared in src/styles/tokens.css
fonts.note: There is no display face by design. Hierarchy comes from size, weight, tracking and case.
fonts.rampNote: Eight steps, closed. Every font-size in all nine stylesheets resolves through a --f-* token; grep finds no pixel literal outside var(--f…). The former --f-return 32px step was deleted rather than kept as reserved, because no surface rendered it.

shadows.name: slip-lift
shadows.purpose: The endorsement slip (toast), and nothing else in the system. It floats over the folio rather than belonging to it, so it is allowed an offset with soft blur. Structural shadow is refused everywhere else.

shadows.name: dialog-scrim
shadows.purpose: Not a shadow. The dialog slip deliberately has no shadow: an ink overlay plus a 1px frame and a 3px head rule do the separating.

shadows.name: struck-entry-inset
shadows.purpose: A drawn rule inside the first cell of a cancelled entry, binding the margin endorsement to its row. box-shadow used as an instrument, not as depth.

focus.name: bracket
focus.purpose: Focus is a bracket, not an outline — two rules flanking the element, drawn behind it with box-shadow so nothing shifts.
focus.fieldVariant: box-shadow: -4px 0 0 0 var(--rule-strong), 4px 0 0 0 var(--rule-strong), inset 0 -2px 0 0 var(--rule-strong) — fields already carry a frame, so they are bracketed outside it and get an inset bottom rule inside it.
invertedRequiredFor: any new filled or dark-field control
focus.mandatory: A rule-strong bracket is invisible on a rule-strong fill. Filled actions must invert theirs to paper inside dark, or focus vanishes into their own fill. This is the protected floor: keyboard first.
focus.compositeVariant: A ruled composite field (the search rule) brackets the whole field on :focus-within and suppresses the inner input's own bracket.

motion.name: stamp
motion.purpose: A press. Buttons translateY(1px) on :active; background and colour changes. A stamp is pressed, it does not glow.

motion.name: draw
motion.purpose: A rule being drawn: the toast slip-in, and the strike fading its decoration colour onto a cancelled entry.

motion.name: rule-sweep
motion.purpose: The waiting state: a 38%-wide rule swept across a 3px track. Loading is a rule being drawn, never a spinning circle.

motion.name: rule-pulse
motion.purpose: In-button loading: a 2px rule scaling on X from 0.2 to 1 from its left origin.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion the world snaps. Nothing is left mid-draw.

extensions.motionGrammar: Stamping and ruling only: discrete, damped, single-axis, one authored moment per surface. No spinners, pulses, bounces, glows or multi-axis transitions.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Folio padding tightens, table cells tighten, the register drops to 720px min-width with a 112px margin column, the off-screen-columns hint appears, the grace bar narrows to 96px, the sign-out label goes visually hidden.

breakpoints.name: sheet
breakpoints.purpose: The dashboard returns and the signin counter sheet collapse from two columns to one; the counter notice's left hairline becomes a top hairline.

grid.note: Nothing on the page is placed off the division grid. The legacy --space-* aliases survive only to feed the .mt-/.mb-/.gap- utilities.

ruleWeights.name: division
ruleWeights.purpose: A section division, and a table's outer bracket.

ruleWeights.name: sheet-head
ruleWeights.purpose: The head rule of a sheet or slip. Vermilion when the slip cancels something.

hatch.name: hatch
hatch.purpose: Elapsing or remaining time, drawn to scale.

hatch.name: hatch-vermilion
hatch.purpose: A lapse. Fills the track rather than emptying it.

declined.name: Visible leader
declined.description: A drawn leader tying a margin endorsement to its entry. Declined, not missing. The binding that ships is the shared row band plus the inset vermilion rule on the first cell.

declined.name: Blind emboss for attested
declined.description: A blind-emboss mark for attested status. Removed because the households list endpoint returns no claim status; booked to return with the household detail page, which has claimStatus.

measuredContrast.note: Measured on the shipped build and recorded as fact. No accessibility standard has been adopted for this product; these are measurements, not a compliance claim.

values.pair: vermilion on the struck row band

composed: /console — the returns and the standing obligation
scope.note: The inherited surfaces get this world through element selectors in src/styles/console.css. Their current appearance is base setting, not designed layout.

components.name: Primary Action
components.description: A filled stamp: the one primary act on a folio, which sits in the folio head. Focus inverts to paper inside dark or it disappears into the fill.

narrative.overview:
A household is a registered title, and this console is the only hand allowed to write on the register. So the page is ruled, not composed. Structure is carried by engraved blue-gray hairlines and full-strength division rules on ledger-bone stock; there are no cards, no status pills, no rounded corners, and no shadow anywhere in the page's own structure. The one authored motion per surface is a stamp being pressed or a rule being drawn.

Density is high and unapologetically clerical: a 6px division governs every measure, numerals are tabular everywhere on the page, and labels are tracked caps set in the rule colour so they read as printed stamps rather than UI chrome. Type is a single face — Libre Franklin, self-hosted variable woff2, weights 400–700, two Latin subsets, SIL OFL — with no display face by design. Hierarchy comes from size, weight, tracking and case, never from a second voice.

State is a mark before it is a hue. A cancelled entry is ruled through in vermilion and stays fully legible; remaining grace is a hatched bar whose length is the actual time left; an entry in good standing leaves the margin blank on purpose, so scanning the margin alone finds every household that needs an operator. The register also prints its own law: the notation key on the households folio draws each mark exactly as the entries draw it.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled, never boxed: divisions are 1px hairlines and 2px full-strength rules, never containers.
One face, tabular figures, tracked-caps stamps for every label and column head.
A closed three-meaning colour law; vermilion means cancellation and nothing else.
Every state readable in grayscale, because geometry carries it and colour only confirms.
Duration drawn to scale rather than restated as prose.
Flat by structure: exactly one shadowed element in the whole system, and it is not page structure.

rules.name: The Closed Law Rule
rules.body: The palette has exactly three meanings: blue-gray = structure and interaction (including focus), iron-gall ink = content, vermilion = struck, cancelled, or in error. There is no fourth. Introducing a hue with a new meaning breaks the system, not just the palette — and the notation key on the register will start lying.

rules.name: The Reserved Red Rule
rules.body: Vermilion is never decoration, never emphasis, never "important". If the thing is not cancelled, expired, or an error, it is drawn in rule or ink.

rules.name: The Mark-Before-Hue Rule
rules.body: Every state is carried by geometry first — strike-through, hatch length, vermilion hatch fill, stamp border, margin hairline, focus bracket — so it survives grayscale and colour blindness. Colour only confirms what the mark already said. Audit test: screenshot in grayscale; if a state disappears, it was never designed.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: There is no display face and no second family. If a heading needs more presence, it gets size, weight, or tracking — not a different typeface.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Numerals are tabular everywhere, set once on body. Never introduce proportional figures into a column, a count, or a date.

rules.name: The Closed Ramp Rule
rules.body: Eight steps, and nothing lives outside them: figure 21 / title 19 / head 17 / entry 15.5 / body 14.5 / caption 12.5 / micro 11.5 / stamp 10.5. Every font-size in every stylesheet resolves through a --f-* token; a literal pixel size is a defect, and a step no surface renders is deleted rather than kept as "reserved" (the former 32px return step went that way). A new size is a deliberate addition to the ramp, never a local override.

rules.name: The Stamp Rule
rules.body: Anything that labels rather than states — column head, field label, action, badge, section head — is tracked caps at stamp size in the rule colour. Sentence-case labels in ink read as content and break the register.

rules.name: The Division Rule
rules.body: Every measure is a multiple of 6px, taken from the division tokens. A hand-typed spacing value is a defect.

rules.name: The Blank Margin Rule
rules.body: The margin column notes exceptions only. An entry in good standing shows a 14px hairline and nothing else, so the margin can be scanned on its own to find every household that needs an operator. Never fill the margin with an "OK" state.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: The toast is the only shadowed thing, because it is the only thing that is not part of the folio. Everything else earns separation from rules, weight and stock.

rules.name: The Bracket Focus Rule
rules.body: Focus is a bracket, not an outline: two rule-strong rules flanking the element, drawn with box-shadow so nothing shifts. Fields keep their own frame and add an inset underline. Filled actions must invert the bracket to paper (paper bracket inside a wider rule-strong bracket), because a rule-strong bracket vanishes into a rule-strong fill. Any new filled or dark-field control inherits this obligation. A ruled composite field (the search rule) brackets the whole field on :focus-within and suppresses the inner input's own bracket. forced-colors falls back to a 2px system outline.

rules.name: The No Radius Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this system is rounded. A radius, however small, reads as a card and cards are refused.

rules.name: The Drawn Duration Rule
rules.body: Time is drawn to scale: the grace bar's length is the real remaining fraction, and a lapsed grace fills the track with the vermilion hatch rather than emptying it — an empty box reads as a failed render, a full one reads as a verdict. Never restate a duration in prose where it can be drawn (the accessible label carries the numbers).

dos: Do draw structure with rules and stock: 1px hairline for column and row divisions, 1px full rule under a table head, 2px rule-strong for a division or a table's outer bracket, 3px for a sheet's head.
Do place every measure on the 6px division scale.
Do label with stamps: tracked caps (0.15em) at 10.5px in the rule colour, for column heads, field labels, buttons, badges and section heads.
Do carry state as a mark first — strike, hatch, border, hairline — and let colour merely confirm it.
Do draw duration to scale, and fill a lapsed track with the vermilion hatch instead of emptying it.
Do bracket focus with box-shadow, and invert the bracket to paper on any filled or dark-field control.

Do keep motion to stamping and ruling: 90ms linear for a press, 320ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) for a draw, one authored moment per surface, single-axis and damped, snapping under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do show waiting as a rule being drawn or a ruled-but-unwritten folio.
Do keep a cancelled entry fully legible while it is struck.
donts: Don't add a fourth colour meaning. Blue-gray, ink, vermilion — that is the whole law, and the notation key prints it.
Don't use vermilion for anything but struck, cancelled, or in error. Not for emphasis, not for a primary action, not for a warning that isn't a cancellation.
Don't introduce a radius, a card, a status pill, or a metric tile. A badge is a bordered stamp; a division is a rule.
Don't shadow page structure. The toast is the only shadowed element in the system.
Don't add a second typeface or a display face, and don't let proportional numerals into a figure column.
Don't write a pixel font-size literal; take a step from the eight-step ramp, or add a step to it deliberately.
Don't use an outline for focus, or a bracket in rule-strong on a rule-strong fill — focus disappears.
Don't ship a spinning circle, a pulse, a bounce, or a multi-axis transition.
Don't fill the margin column for entries in good standing; a blank margin is the reading.
Don't restate in prose a duration the page can draw, and don't empty a track to signal a lapse.
Don't reflow the register into cards at narrow widths; scroll the ledger and announce the off-screen columns.
declined: The visible leader tying a margin endorsement to its entry was declined; the shared row band plus the inset vermilion rule on the first cell is the binding that ships.
The blind emboss for attested was removed because the households list endpoint returns no claim status; it is booked to return with the household detail page, which has claimStatus.
